extracted.intended_audience: media researchers, journalists, policymakers, and news-industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Country profile summarising the Italian media system: audience metrics, market structure, revenue trends, ownership changes, trust, and press-freedom indicators. Intended to provide evidence-based diagnostics of the news ecosystem in Italy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic demographic context used to scale other media metrics and market size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of potential digital audience reach and the scope for online news consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly reach for TV news
rubrics_metrics.description: Weekly reach for TV news has declined from 85% in 2017 to 65% in 2024; among 18–24-year-olds just 50% use TV for news weekly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess television's role as a primary news source and age-related shifts in news consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television market concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Market concentration: the three major broadcasters (PSB RAI, Sky, Mediaset) account for approximately three-quarters of total revenues in the television sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of competitive diversity in TV broadcasting and potential implications for plurality and market power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of advertising revenues by medium
rubrics_metrics.description: By 2022 online advertising accounted for 58% of overall advertising revenues, with television 29% and print 5%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows structural shift in advertising expenditure across media; relevant for assessing financial health and business model viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers' share of digital advertising revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers generate just 15% of digital advertising revenues, while online platforms such as Alphabet/Google and Meta/Facebook garner 85%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights imbalance between tech platforms and news publishers in capturing digital ad value; explains why online ad growth may not rescue news organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper circulation decline
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent decline in copies sold: -37% from 2019 to 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core indicator of print market decline; used alongside advertising and distribution metrics to evaluate newspaper sector crisis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper sector responses (paywalls and membership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most newspapers implemented paywalls; some digital-native outlets (Il Post, Open, Linkiesta) have introduced membership models. Digital replicas of printed newspapers are prioritised because they are priced higher than access via websites/apps, but they account for a tiny proportion of sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes common publisher strategies to monetise audiences and their limited effectiveness as evidenced by low uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion paying for online news
rubrics_metrics.description: Our survey shows just 10% pay for online news each week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct consumer-payment metric indicating willingness to subscribe or pay — key for assessing sustainability of paid models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rise of digital-born outlets and online reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital-born outlets (e.g., Fanpage, Il Post) have recently challenged established players; Fanpage returned in 2024 to lead online brand reach in the survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals changing competitive dynamics online and importance of social-media-led distribution for audience reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper market concentration and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: GEDI and Cairo/RCS jointly account for 38% of total copies sold in 2023; other publishers each contribute less than 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess concentration in the print sector and implications for plurality and market power among publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership changes and editorial strategy shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: GEDI's acquisition by the Agnelli-Elkann family led to sales of flagship titles and perceived softening of La Repubblica's centre-left stance; journalists protested proposed sales of local outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links ownership changes to editorial positioning, staff responses (strikes), and potential effects on audience trust and diversity of viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Takeovers and political/business ownership concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Centre-right newspaper takeovers (e.g., Antonio Angelucci buying Il Giornale) and negotiations to acquire AGI have sparked concerns and strikes among journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights political and business influence risks from concentrated or politically-aligned ownership and associated newsroom reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline in physical distribution (news kiosks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly 2,700 news kiosks disappeared across the country in four years, with a total of approximately 13,500 by 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of weakening offline distribution channels and added strain on print viability and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy change: ending legal advertising obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: From January 2024 the obligation to publish tender and public contract information in newspapers ('legal advertising') ended, posing a revenue loss estimated at around €40m annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how regulatory changes can directly affect newspaper revenues and the economic environment for publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news overall
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in news remains low at 34% (score = 31/47).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate trust metric used to evaluate public confidence in news; broken down by brand partisanship and perceived impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of partisanship on brand trust
rubrics_metrics.description: The most trusted brands are generally those seen as less partisan, while those with a clear partisan bias tend to command lower trust; lower scores for digital-born players may be because they have had less time to build a reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative explanatory criterion linking perceived partisanship and brand age/reputation to trust levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: RSF World Press Freedom Index
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF World Press Freedom Index: rank 46/180, Score 69.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International press-freedom benchmark to situate the country's media freedom context; based on Reporters Without Borders assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to podcast in the last month: 32%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience engagement metric for audio formats; relevant to assessing diversification of news consumption habits.
